May 2026.
One tweet, written in Morse code,
told an AI agent to
send about a hundred and fifty
thousand dollars to a stranger.
The agent obeyed.
Agents now hold wallets,
and they read the internet.
Whoever writes that text
can steer the money.
Allowlists check where funds go.
Simulators check what a transaction does.
Nobody records who decided.
This is TAINT.
A wallet for AI agents
that checks who decided.
Every recipient, token and amount
carries its provenance: it came from you,
or from outside text.
The planner never sees attacker text,
only opaque handles.
A separate extractor turns outside content
into typed values,
and anything that doesn't parse never becomes one.
Each argument is stamped
either owner or untrusted.
Then a NEAR contract
enforces the rule.
Owner-decided values pass, within caps.
Untrusted ones are held
for your co-sign.
On NEAR, every owner gets
their own account in the policy contract,
with their own balance,
address book and caps.
Runs are signed with NEP-413.
Co-signs can be relayed
with NEP-366 delegate actions.
And inference runs on
NEAR AI Cloud,
with response signatures that we check.
The worker's TEE attestation is still stubbed,
and we say so.
Against a real model,
the naive agent was drained in
twenty out of twenty attacks.
TAINT executed none of them.
Security, because it stops the drain.
Agents, because the agent
can still read everything.
Privacy, because inference runs
on confidential models.
Real world, because it is
live on testnet today.
Live, on testnet.
I connect my own wallet
and run the Morse-code tweet.
Three agents read the same text.
TAINT holds the payment,
and shows the source: x.com/@attacker.
I review it on the co-sign page,
and approve once.
Only then does the contract pay.
This is my wallet page:
my balance, my caps,
and a pause switch.
To get started,
deposit your funds into your TAINT wallet.
You set the limits,
and you can pause or
withdraw at any time.
